data.name: evaluation_description
data.value: Enumerate every remaining opportunity to make the workflow-server `meta` and `work-package` workflows faster and cheaper to run, measured against the build as it stands after the optimisation work merged on 2026-08-17/18 (server PRs #467, #471; definition PRs #468, #470). The 2026-08-17 evaluation report at .engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-08-17-meta-and-work-package-workflow-optimisation/EVALUATION-REPORT.md is the worked example for shape and rigour, and explicitly not the boundary of what may be found. Both halves of the complaint are in scope: token cost and wall-clock latency.

value.description: What the recent optimisation work actually changed and what it measurably bought, so that 'remaining' is measured against the current build rather than against the prior report.
focus_areas: Re-measure the benchmark walk against the recorded baseline and attribute the 26.8% fall from 1,780,292 to 1,302,319 delivery characters to specific changes
Which of the prior report's 52 findings (15 high, 27 medium, 10 low) are closed, which partly addressed, which untouched
Whether gate-liveness bundling (src/utils/gate-liveness.ts) reduced the permanently-lazy step counts (89 of 174 in work-package, 12 of 23 in meta) against the 83 and 19 when-gated steps counted today
Whether the delivery-cost gate in .github/workflows/verify.yml runs, and whether its resolution distinguishes the changes it guards from noise
The workflow-version drift exposure on resumed sessions, named as the largest risk in the prior report: closed, mitigated, or open
Regressions introduced by the remediation itself
value.name: Remediation Effect

value.description: The bytes still shipped into agent contexts per run, and the abstraction that would collapse each remaining duplication.
focus_areas: get_resource as the largest bucket: 527,683 characters over 162 calls, 146 fetches against 77 distinct ledger keys
get_activity at 520,075 characters over 12 calls; the eager bundling budget and per-activity size caps
get_workflow at 108,356 characters in one call at session open
Content bundled then refetched: a technique bundled into get_activity does not satisfy a later standalone get_technique for the same body
Inherited-input and rules blocks restated per technique across 262 technique files
Resources delivered whole where a step reads one section, and sections fetched repeatedly where the whole file would serve
Prose in the 909 KB corpus that restates what schemas/ already enforces
value.name: Delivery Economy

value.description: How the run is distributed across agents, turns and round trips, and what sets its wall-clock — the 'slow' half of the brief, which the prior report addressed only through byte counts.
focus_areas: 242 tool calls for a 12-activity walk: which sit on the critical path, which could be batched, elided or made concurrent
The batch bound still at defaults (BATCH_MAX_ACTIVITIES 3, BATCH_HEADROOM_FRACTION 0.35) — re-measure what raising it buys now delivery is 26.8% smaller

Checkpoint density and placement: 44 gates in work-package across 13 of 15 activities (10 in 01-start-work-package, 9 in 13-submit-for-review, 0 in 11-validate and 14-complete), 5 in meta with 3 in 00-discover-session
10 yield/respond/resume triples per walk, each a full context handover
Serial steps that could run concurrently; sub-agent spawn and context re-establishment at every activity boundary
Sequential model turns as the dominant wall-clock term, weighed against per-call server latency
value.name: Orchestration Topology and Critical Path

value.description: Protocol steps in the ~117,000 words of agent-executed prose that are deterministic procedures a script or server tool could compute, re-priced against the cost instrument that now exists.
focus_areas: The 12 candidates the prior run identified: still present, and now measurable against a CI cost gate that did not exist then
Repo/component/issue/PR coordinate resolution, path derivation, project-type detection, artifact link and anchor checking, Progress-table writes, git and worktree state checks
Classification steps that are fixed decision tables
18 registered tools, all session control-plane: whether a domain-computation tool is the right home for each candidate, or a script, or a definition edit
28 check-*.ts guards reachable only as CI, never as a workflow operation
For each candidate, whether the prose hides a judgement call
value.name: Mechanisation Potential

value.description: Steps, artifacts and verification the workflows perform that produce nothing the run consumes.
focus_areas: Activities and techniques never reached in practice across meta's 5 activities and work-package's 15
Artifacts written but never read downstream
Verification repeated at multiple stages: 28 check-*.ts guards alongside in-workflow verify-artifact-conforms and the validators
Optional branches that always resolve the same way — the remediation closed four gates that cannot open; whether more remain
Duplication across the two trees, including parallel TECHNIQUE.md group files and shared technique basenames
Rare-but-load-bearing paths distinguished from genuinely dead ones
value.name: Redundant Work

value.description: What each remaining opportunity costs to build, what it risks, and the order the opportunities should be taken in.
focus_areas: Implementation surface per opportunity: a server change in src/ (12,628 LOC, 18 tools), a script under scripts/ (47 files, 9,935 LOC), or a definition edit in the 909 KB corpus
Guard and test coverage protecting each change (82 test files, 18,955 LOC; 28 guards; the new tests/gate-liveness.test.ts and scripts/check-decision-order.ts)
Saved-session and backwards compatibility for sessions holding an older definition shape
Whether each saving is resolvable by the CI cost gate or falls below its noise floor
The submodule boundary: definitions land in the workflows submodule, server changes in the superproject, and a paired change needs both
Sequencing dependencies, and which costs are immovable regardless of redesign
value.name: Change Economics

data.name: scope_summary
data.value: Target /home/mike1/projects/dev/workflow-server (workflow-server), classified mixed — package.json and tsconfig.json make it a codebase, and the subject of the evaluation is 909 KB / ~117,000 words of definition markdown carried in the workflows git submodule. Output directory .engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-08-18-optimisation-of-meta-and-work-package-workflows, created and verified writable. Pipeline mode full-prism; no lens overrides supplied; six dimensions derived (none supplied by the user): Remediation Effect, Delivery Economy, Orchestration Topology and Critical Path, Mechanisation Potential, Redundant Work, Change Economics. Measured starting position: workflows/meta 171 files (160 md, 11 yaml), 291 KB, ~37,961 words, 5 activities, 23 technique steps, 5 checkpoints, 19 when-gated steps; workflows/work-package 168 files (152 md), 619 KB, ~79,032 words, 15 activities, 176 technique steps, 44 checkpoints, 83 when-gated steps; src/ 55 TypeScript files, 12,628 LOC, 18 registered MCP tools all session control-plane; scripts/ 47 files, 9,935 LOC including 28 check-*.ts guards; tests/ 82 files, 18,955 LOC. Recorded benchmark walk (12 activities, fresh context): 1,302,319 delivery characters over 242 tool calls — get_resource 162 calls / 527,683 chars / 146 fetches against 77 distinct ledger keys, get_activity 12 calls / 520,075 chars with 66 techniques bundled and 24 fetched separately, get_technique 24 calls / 146,205 chars, get_workflow 1 call / 108,356 chars, plus 10 yield/respond/resume triples. Delivery trajectory 1,355,532 (July) to 1,780,292 (2026-08-17, pre-remediation) to 1,302,319 (now). Recent remediation: 42 files, 1,861 insertions, 297 deletions across server PRs #467 and #471 and definition PRs #468 and #470. Batch bound still at defaults: BATCH_MAX_ACTIVITIES 3, BATCH_HEADROOM_FRACTION 0.35.
